seoTitle: How to Duplicate a Project in Asana Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to copy an entire Asana project in 2026, choosing which tasks and fields to carry over, and shift due dates to match a new timeline.
intro: Rebuilding a recurring campaign board from scratch wastes hours you don't have, and Asana's duplicate feature can copy an entire project structure in a few clicks. This guide covers opening the duplication panel, choosing which elements to carry over, and shifting dates to match your new kickoff.

steps.heading: Open the project dropdown menu
steps.body: Go to your source project and find the dropdown header menu next to the project name.

steps.heading: Select Duplicate Project
steps.body: Choose the duplicate option to launch the configuration panel for copying the project.

steps.heading: Choose which elements to include
steps.body: Decide whether to carry over tasks, milestones, assignees, due dates, custom fields, and attachments, or leave certain details behind.

steps.heading: Set the new project details
steps.body: Give the duplicate a new name, choose its team space, and set the appropriate privacy permissions.

steps.heading: Shift dates and verify the copy
steps.body: Use the date shifting tool to align milestones with your new project timeline, then review the newly generated board to confirm everything copied correctly.

faq.question: Can I duplicate a project without copying task assignees?
faq.answer: Yes, the duplication panel lets you deselect assignees so the new project starts unassigned if you prefer.

faq.question: Will custom fields carry over to the duplicated project?
faq.answer: Yes, you can choose to include custom fields as part of the elements copied into the new project.

faq.question: Does duplicating a project shift all the due dates automatically?
faq.answer: Only if you use the date shifting tool during setup, which recalculates milestones relative to your new project start date.

faq.question: Can I use a duplicated project as a reusable template?
faq.answer: Yes, many teams duplicate a clean template project repeatedly to standardize recurring campaigns or client onboarding workflows.
